## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```
```{r}
plot(cars)
```

## GGPLOT Plots

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(cars) +
  aes(x = speed, y = dist) +
  geom_point() +
  ggtitle("Title")
```

## Artificial Data

This is one way to order months.
Note that the first plot orders alphabetically,
while the second plot following the use of `ordered()`
gets them in the right order.

```{r}
dat <- data.frame(
  month = c("January", "February", "March"),
  value = c(1.5, 2.5, 7)
)
ggplot(dat) +
  aes(month, value) +
  geom_point()
```

```{r}
dat$month <- ordered(dat$month, c("January", "February", "March"))
ggplot(dat) +
  aes(month, value) +
  geom_point()
```

For more on dates and times see
[Dates and Times](README.md/#dates-and-times).

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=TRUE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
